newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-WANG TAO LOSES UNBEATEN RECORD.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-WANG TAO LOSES UNBEATEN RECORD.

text.p: Frenchman Jean-Philippe Gatien, the 1993 champion, scored an upset fourth victory over Chinese world number six Wang Tao on Saturday to reach the quarter-finals of the men's singles at the world table tennis championships.

Gatien won the battle of the left-handers 21-19 21-17 21-14 in a match of blistering rallies. The 29-year-old Wang, a silver medallist at the Atlanta Olympics, was the only Chinese player to stay unbeaten throughout the team competition.
The two men did not meet in last Wednesday's team final, which China won 3-1.
Gatien was bracketed in the 9-16 seeds, while Wang was in the 5-8 bracket.

The victory earned Gatien a match against another former winner, 1989 champion Jan-Ove Waldner. The second-seeded Swede had a comparatively easy passage against Croatian Zoran Primorac, coasting home 21-16 21-13 21-13.

Waldner, 31, the 1992 Olympic gold medallist, has been steadily tightening his game after Sweden's disappointing team performance and has a fine world championship record having twice been a finalist in addition to his 1989 triumph.
World number four Vladimir Samsonov of Belarus is the only other non-Chinese player in the last eight.
Samsonov showed his resilience in earning a hard-fought 21-16 10-21 24-22 21-19 victory over Wang Liqin, the Chinese youngster who eliminated Sweden's 1991 world champion Jorgen Persson.
Samsonov trailed 10-17 in the third set and 12-18 in the next, making up the deficit in both cases by effective counter-hitting.
In the next round he faces another unseeded Chinese, Ding Song who outplayed Milan Grman of Slovakia.

Chinese defending champion Kong Linghui did not have things all his own way, dropping a set in seeing off Austrian Werner Schlager 21-16 22-20 17-21 21-18. He next faces compatriot Ma Weng, who outlasted Japanese defensive slice specialist Hiroshi Shibutani 21-19 21-17 17-21 21-17.
The other quarter-final matches Spanish-based former Chinese international He Zhe Wen and Yan Sen of China, who defeated another ex-China mainland player, Johnny Huang of Canada.
German European champion Nicole Struse is the only non-Chinese player in the women's quarter-finals, having defeated joint-fifth seed Wang Chen of China.
The biggest upset was the defeat of second-seeded Chen Jing, the 1988 Olympic champion who defected from China and won a silver medal representing Taiwan at the 1996 Atlanta Games.
The left-hander succumbed to Wu Na 25-23 21-14 21-12.
Deng Yaping, the reigning world and Olympic champion, reached the last eight without dropping a set and faces unseeded Wong Ching, who moved from mainland China to Hong Kong a year ago.
